frictionSummary: Custom apps are instant and store-specific; public apps go through App Store review.
prerequisites: A Shopify Partner account (free) and access to the Shopify Dev Dashboard
Since Jan 2026, new custom apps must be created via the Dev Dashboard or Partner Dashboard, not the store admin — and now go through an OAuth flow like public apps, rather than a copyable admin token
For a public app: a design and billing flow (via the Billing API) ready for Shopify's review

steps.title: Decide: custom app or public app
steps.body: Custom apps target one store (or a small, known set) and skip the App Store entirely. Public apps use OAuth 2.0 and can be installed on any store, but must pass Shopify's App Store review before public listing.

steps.title: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard
steps.body: As of January 2026, Shopify no longer allows creating custom apps from the store admin UI — both custom and public apps are created via the Shopify Dev Dashboard (or Partner Dashboard).

steps.title: Request scopes and complete the OAuth flow
steps.body: Redirect the merchant to the shop's authorize URL, then exchange the returned code for an access token.

steps.title: If going public, submit for App Store review
steps.body: Reviewers test the full install/authorization flow end-to-end and expect the Billing API wired up correctly and a UI that holds up under Shopify's design requirements.

approval.expectedWait: None for custom apps (single store); review required only for public App Store listing
approval.notes: Doc-sourced from Shopify's Dev Docs and App Store requirements. A custom app installs directly with no review; a public app must pass App Store review, which tests the full OAuth and billing flow.

gotchas: As of Jan 1, 2026, custom apps can no longer be created from the store admin — use the Dev Dashboard or Partner Dashboard instead, and existing custom apps keep working as-is

New custom apps now go through an OAuth flow to get an access token, where previously you could copy a long-lived token directly from the admin UI — this changes integration code that assumed a static token
Installing one "custom" app across many unrelated stores outside the App Store may run into Shopify's Terms of Service — custom apps are meant for a single merchant or a small known set
Public apps need the Billing API wired up correctly, not just OAuth, before they'll pass review

do: Install @shopify/shopify-api for the OAuth + Admin API flow
Add placeholder env vars: SHOPIFY_API_KEY, SHOPIFY_API_SECRET, SHOPIFY_REDIRECT_URI, SHOPIFY_SCOPES
Wire up install redirect to https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize with the minimum scopes needed
Verify the HMAC signature on the callback request before exchanging the code, per Shopify's security requirements
dont: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard or submit for App Store review — that's the developer's call
Enter the real API secret anywhere — leave it as an env placeholder
Assume a long-lived token can be copied from the admin UI for new custom apps — that path is gone as of Jan 2026
